intro.say: Missing tools, a missing voice, a missing font, and source that has moved.

chapters.title: Ask the doctor
chapters.say: A render will not start. Now what?

beats.say: One command checks the four things a render needs.
beats.mark: checks the Python packages, ffmpeg, the browser and the voice model

beats.say: For each one that is missing, it names a ready-made video that explains the fix.
So even the error message arrives as a video.
beats.mark: sends that video instead of an error message

beats.say: Install ffmpeg with your package manager, and a browser with one command.
The Python packages come from the requirements file.
And the voice model can be dropped into its cache folder by hand.

chapters.title: No voice, no font
chapters.say: What if only the voice is missing, or a font?

beats.say: Without the voice model, a silent render still makes the video, and the captions carry the narration.
If the machine cannot draw some characters, the render says which ones, and a font that covers them fixes it.
beats.mark: installing a font that covers them

chapters.title: It will not show what is not there
chapters.say: And when the error is about the source itself?

beats.say: The engine refuses to show something that is not there.
beats.mark: refuses to show something that is not there

beats.say: If a file changed and the lines have moved, the check stops, and says which scene and why.
This is that guard. Every code scene says what its first line should contain.
If the file no longer agrees, the render stops here instead of showing the wrong lines.
So an error like this is the tool keeping its promise.
